Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

prospect noun

a chance of something in the future

also prospects, future prospects, in prospect, there is little prospect of

classical

Cic. Fam. 14.4.3: sī est spēs nostrī reditūs

spēs, speī f.

noun, fifth declension

hope, prospect

A good prospect is a hope: spēs with a genitive of what is hoped for. It is the everyday word for hope (see hope).

Other words

  • exspectātiō, exspectātiōnis f. — expectation, what is looked for

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 4.80: sī spēs est exspectātiō bonī, malī exspectātiōnem esse necesse est metum (Lewis & Short)

    The waiting for something, good or bad; a bad prospect is a fear, metus.

Examples

  • sī est spēs nostrī reditūs, eam cōnfīrmēs et rem adjuvēs

    if there is any prospect of my return, strengthen it and help the matter alongCic. Fam. 14.4.3

  • cum in spem magis futūrae multitūdinis quam ad id quod tum hominum erat mūnīrent

    for they built their walls for the prospect of a future population rather than for the people they had thenLiv. 1.8.4

See also hope, possibility, future, view.

SourcesLewis & Short: spes · Lewis & Short: exspectatio
